html:
Envuga is the name the map gives to a Kawahib group in the forests of central Rondônia, in western Brazil. Little is recorded about a group of this name. The Kawahib speak languages of the Tupi-Guarani branch of the Tupian family and were once one people, who split into many groups as they moved through the Madeira basin.

Other Kawahib include the Jupaú of Rondônia, the Tenharim and the Parintintin. Rubber tappers, and from the 1970s road building and ranching, pressed all of them hard.
